status: DESIGN APPENDIX v3 (backlog): rows for milestones M3-M5 and 'post'. Not loaded by the game and not gated by the data test; a row moves into the live file, and under test, when its milestone starts. Rows may reference live ids.
summary: The five other backgrounds, revised; the backcountry hunter's M5 start variants; other starts.
id_rules: Ids are stable strings (prefix.name). Never rename an id once saves exist; add an alias instead. Display names are separate and may change. An id is defined in exactly one place: the live file or the backlog.

milestones.M1: A winter night: fire, shelter, cold, hunger, sleep, time safety; the fort region only; one background; 1765
milestones.M2a: A winter from the woods: living from the manor woods through the winter by your own hands (gathering, hides, sewing, snares, snowshoes, a half-faced camp, a hung cache, ice fishing); plain barter with the sutler, the trader, the garrison's soldiers, a farm family from German Flatts and an old hunter; credit and the fall outfit as options; the second background
milestones.M2b: Learning from neighbours: lessons, watching, examining, quality standards, haggling, promises and loans
milestones.M3: The year turns: the full almanac, seasons and weather content, the summer goal (bark and a cabin), fishing, frogs, ginseng, one played wage job; the fur cap and robe, leggings, carving, casting balls, the cache pit, char cloth and spruce beer
milestones.M4: People: NPC schedules and tiers at the fort, standing, invitations, the soldiers and the lieutenant as mentors; Native characters only after the relevant nation's sign-off
milestones.M5: The map: the Carry, the valley, the town and the hunting grounds, travel and camps, other markets and backgrounds
milestones.post: After M5 and not yet planned: the 1757 and 1761 starts and their eras, detailed illnesses, thirst, potash, upstream canoe and bateau travel, the Proxy NPC tier, languages beyond English, French, Mohawk and Oneida

backgrounds.name: Valley settler (tenant or freeholder)
backgrounds.life_history: Farms a lot in the Mohawk valley, leased from a patentee or bought from one, and turns out with the county militia or supplies it when called.
backgrounds.historical_basis: New York land came through patents, manor and patent leases and purchase from patentees, not a warrant office. The valley held Palatine German, Dutch and Scots-Irish families (review 1, issue 1).

choose_one.name: Dutch family of the Hudson and Mohawk
Freeholder who bought from a patentee

perk.text: Starts with a lot, seed corn and salt; salting and cabin work +0.05.

drawback.text: Rent or purchase balance due each November, and the militia calls. Men answer musters; women supply the muster, hold the blockhouse and host refugees in alarms (option: open musters, documented as fiction).

backgrounds.budget_note: v3 budget (100-105 over the v3 roster); restated to the v4 budget of 145-155 over the ten skills, with no experience multiplier, when this background's milestone starts (GDD 12)

backgrounds.name: Raised in a town of the nations
backgrounds.milestone_gate: M5, after consultation with the nation's cultural office (survival_gdd.md 20.9)
backgrounds.life_history: Born or adopted into a household of a town of the chosen nation; learned the household's round of fields, the fall hunt, spring fishing and sugaring, and the town's trade with posts and settlers.
backgrounds.historical_basis: Haudenosaunee towns stayed occupied through the year; men went on the fall hunt and returned for Midwinter; women held the fields (N:6, N:7, E:S44). Adoption into households followed captivity, condolence or politics (E:S35).
backgrounds.rule: An upbringing, not an ancestry: any body, skin tone, face or sex may take it, and choosing it never changes appearance. Its skills come from training in a household's round; it does not top every survival stat.

home_town.note: The only town on the map is modelled on Kanonwalohale: an Oneida town with Tuscarora families living among the Oneida.

home_town_when_regions_exist.mohawk: Canajoharie or Tiononderoge, when those regions exist

kin_by_marriage_or_adoption.rule: A character of another nation living in the Oneida town as kin by marriage or adoption: own language (lang), the host town's culture data.

deferred.to: future regions (node.west, node.north); not selectable until then

nation.rule: Nations are not interchangeable skins: the town's culture data is the Oneida town's, and other nations appear only where history places them (review 1 of v2, major 4).

household_focus.note: Chosen freely; not tied to the character's sex.

perk.text: A household in the home town: lodging and meals with it, speaks the language, knows the household's hunting grounds.

drawback.text: No colonial money at the start (goods instead). The household expects meat in the hungry time (Feb-Mar) and your hands in its round: harvest, the fall hunt, sugaring. Each missed obligation costs standing that grows each time, and two in a row end free lodging until made good.

obligation.two_misses: free lodging suspended until one obligation is made good

backgrounds.name: Discharged regular soldier
backgrounds.life_history: Served in a regular regiment (British) or the troupes de la Marine (French) and stayed in the country.
backgrounds.historical_basis: Regular rations, drill and camp medicine (Pringle, K:7); the 1763 Proclamation offered land to discharged soldiers.
suggested_presets: Troupes de la marine, winter campaign

choose_one.name: Troupes de la Marine
choose_one.lock_reason: Before the conquest a French soldier cannot start at a British fort; unlocks in 1761 and later starts, or when a Canadien parish or Oswegatchie region exists.

choose_one.name: On a regiment's ration list: a soldier's wife, laundress or nurse

perk.text: Knows how a garrison runs: +25% on the sutler's meat channel and the firewood contract, and a ration (one meal a day) from the sutler during winter quarters. Starts with a teacher: a backcountry hunter at the post teaches the snow camp at standing 0.

drawback.text: A poor woodsman who owes the sutler 288 d (stoppages and a discharge debt), due in the spring settlement window; in wartime starts the other crown's people distrust you.

backgrounds.v3_note: Survival 20 (was 15) and a perk that works in slice systems (review 2 of v2, the backgrounds issue); the snow-camp teacher is a backcountry hunter, not the ranger lieutenant (review 1 of v2, blocker).
backgrounds.service_note: Regular service was men's service: on the 'historical' setting a woman takes the ration-list variant (a soldier's wife, laundress or nurse on the regiment's ration list); 'open service' is documented fiction (review 1 of v2, minor 19).
backgrounds.budget_note: v3 budget (100-105 over the v3 roster); restated to the v4 budget of 145-155 over the ten skills, with no experience multiplier, when this background's milestone starts (GDD 12)

backgrounds.name: Canadien habitant or voyageur
backgrounds.lock_reason: Before the conquest a Canadien cannot start at a British post; from 1761 Montreal traders under British licence hire Canadien crews (review 1, issue 2).
backgrounds.life_history: From the St. Lawrence parishes; paddles and portages for a Montreal trader and knows winter travel.
backgrounds.historical_basis: Canadian capots, mitts and snowshoe travel (K:4, K:27); Montreal traders under British licence after 1760 hired Canadien crews (E:S25, E:S26).

perk.text: Canoe, bateau and snowshoe routes 10% faster; starts with capot, mitts and tuque.

drawback.text: Engaged to a Montreal trader: deliver a pack of furs (or its value) at the spring trade, or lose the engagement and your credit with the Montreal traders.

start.note: Montreal crews worked the St. Lawrence and Lake Ontario route (Oswegatchie, Niagara, Oswego), not the Carry; a future St. Lawrence region is the natural start.

choose_one.name: A Montreal trader's engagé at Oswego (men's work: voyageurs were men)
A hired hand on an Albany bateau (the Mohawk route)
A habitante trader or sugar-maker from the St. Lawrence parishes

start.rule: Voyageur engagements were men's; on the 'historical' setting a woman takes the habitante variant; 'open service' is documented fiction (review 1 of v2, minors 19 and 20).

backgrounds.name: Trader's clerk or packhorseman
backgrounds.life_history: Kept accounts and drove packhorses for a licensed trader; now trading on a merchant's consignment.
backgrounds.historical_basis: Packhorse trains of about 200 lb a horse (E:S27); credit and licences (E:S7).

perk.text: Market spread -0.05 and credit lines x1.5 at posts and stores.

drawback.text: Owes the Albany merchant for consigned goods; weak in the woods.

choose_one.text: The live start: Cosby's Manor, patented and unsettled; legal, no leave needed.
Hunts the Oneida grounds by the town's leave, granted last season: +5 standing with the town, and a share of meat is expected in the hungry time. Legal by the town's leave.

Hunts the Oneida grounds without leave, as many colonial hunters did after 1763 (a standing Oneida complaint to Johnson): -2 standing per carcass, and the town hunters will ask him to leave. Not legal under the Proclamation and the Oneida's own law.

hunting_grounds_start.rule: The data says whether each start is legal (review 1 of v2, major 2).
